questions.q: What is the core difference between a union and a join?
options: A union stacks rows from multiple tables vertically; a join matches rows on a key and adds columns horizontally
A union adds columns; a join stacks rows
There is no difference — they're two names for the same operation
A union can only combine two tables; a join can combine any number
questions.explain: A union appends one table's rows underneath another's (vertical stacking), while a join combines matching rows into wider rows (horizontal combining).

questions.q: Which SQL construct is Tableau's union functionally equivalent to?
options: UNION ALL — it keeps every row from every table, duplicates included
INNER JOIN
UNION (which removes duplicate rows)
A correlated subquery
questions.explain: Tableau's union behaves like UNION ALL: every row from every included table is kept, without de-duplication.

questions.q: How do you start building a union (rather than a join) in Tableau's data source canvas?
options: Drag a second table directly beneath an existing table, rather than onto it
Right-click the worksheet tab and select Union
Unions can only be created in Tableau Prep, never in Desktop
Type a UNION ALL statement into a custom SQL box
questions.explain: Dragging a table beneath another (a distinct drop target from the join target) starts a union rather than a join.

questions.q: What does a Wildcard (automatic) union do that a manual union doesn't?
options: Automatically includes every table matching a naming pattern, including tables added after the union is built
Removes duplicate rows automatically
Only works with database connections, never Excel or text files
Converts the union into a join automatically
questions.explain: A wildcard union uses a naming pattern (like *2016) so new matching tables are picked up automatically on refresh, without manually re-adding them.

questions.q: What happens if you union two tables where one has a column the other doesn't?
options: The unioned result includes that column, with NULLs for the rows from the table that didn't have it
Tableau refuses to build the union at all
The mismatched column is silently dropped from the result
Tableau automatically renames the column to match
questions.explain: Just like a SQL UNION ALL over tables with mismatched columns, the missing column shows up as NULL for rows from the table that lacked it.
